## Context

The composer the phone exists for: surface 1, built from its artboard as a screen of its own after the first attempt built it as a box inside the session view and had this milestone's own scope row rewritten to match. Multi-line, spell-checked, one draft, and a destination chosen after the writing rather than before it.

## Done means

The box is the screen and the destination row is beneath it: thought first, destination second.
The route row defaults to the last active session, ordered by what tmux reports as activity rather than by name.
The idea inbox is a route beside the sessions, and choosing it files a record under the destination's own prefix rather than typing into anything.
The composer is spell-checked, autocapitalised and autocorrected, and Enter inserts a newline while Send submits.
One draft, under one key shared with the session view's reply box, written as it is typed so a backgrounded phone cannot lose it, and the header says it is kept only when the browser actually kept it.
A send that could not go leaves the text where it was: the server says why on the socket, and the form path hands the draft back with the page.
Multi-line arrives in a session as one message rather than one prompt per line.
The form posts and works with the script blocked.

## Verified against

Real tmux and the real CLI, plus tests. What is asserted rather than measured is labelled as such in MUS-D-0096 and in the source.

The clause no test proves: that a bracketed paste reaches an agent's composer as ONE message rather than one prompt per line. Measured by hand against Claude Code — four lines pasted into a live pane, one Enter, and the agent answered from all four, replying 'ALPHA, BRAVO, CHARLIE' to a message whose first three lines were those words. Plain send-keys also placed all four lines in the composer, which is why the mechanism is argued from reliability rather than from a failure to work.

What the tests prove: multi-line leaves the composer over a real WebSocket and arrives in a real session's input, in order, with its newlines — all three asserted in that one test, after a review found this record crediting it with two checks it did not make. Send uses the bracketed, self-cleaning paste path for multi-line and keystrokes for single-line. The destination row is ordered by activity and pre-selects the most recent, against a listing where the alphabetical answer and the correct one differ. The inbox files under IDW rather than the store's prefix, which caught that an explicitly chosen destination never read its prefix at all. A failed send returns the draft. A page with nowhere to send offers no box and loads no script.

Neither real-tmux test discriminates between paste and keystrokes, because the pane holds cat and cat is happy with newlines either way. Both say so in their own comments.

## Risks

The done-when says from a phone, off the home network, without a terminal. The transport, the multi-line handling and the draft are verified here; the phone, the network and the browser's spell-checker are the owner's to confirm, as 2c's last sentence was.

A message can now be started in three places — the composer, the session view's reply box, and the intake box. MUS-Q-0018 put the reply box there and MUS-D-0013 asks for one capture surface; both are the owner's and they disagree. Reported in queue.md rather than resolved here.

This is the second surface carrying script. The rule was a count of one and is now a count of two, taken deliberately on MUS-Q-0034 and bounded by the form working without it.

Enter-inserts-newline is a change in feel from the box that shipped at 4b, where Enter sent. Nobody has used either from a phone yet.

The draft is per-device, because the server holds no per-client state. A draft started on the phone is not on the laptop.
